# [CS019] Insecure File Permissions (insecure-file-permissions)

A file or directory is created world-writable or a secret file world-readable.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **Severity** | MEDIUM |
| **Category** | Security |
| **CWE** | [CWE-732](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/732.html) |
| **OWASP** | A02:2025 |
| **Auto-Fix supported** | No |

## Why It Matters in Go

Modes such as 0777 or 0666 let every local user modify the file, and 0644 on keys or tokens lets them read it. Use 0600 for secrets and 0750 or 0755 for directories.

## Vulnerable / Problematic Example

```go
os.WriteFile("token", tok, 0o666)
```

## Safe / Idiomatic Go Pattern

```go
os.WriteFile("token", tok, 0o600)
```

## Configuration & Suppression

Disable the rule for the whole module in `.codexsentinel.yaml`:

```yaml
rules:
  disabled: [insecure-file-permissions]
```

Change its severity:

```yaml
rules:
  severity_overrides:
    insecure-file-permissions: low
```

Suppress one reviewed finding on its line, with the reason:

```go
//codex:ignore insecure-file-permissions -- <reason>
```

Or ignore it under a path in `.codexsentinel.ignore`:

```text
internal/legacy/** insecure-file-permissions
```
